title: A 17.7-to-29.5GHz Transceiver Front-End with 3.3dB NF and 20.2dBm OP1dB in 65nm CMOS
problem: Wideband mm-wave transceivers must simultaneously achieve low-noise wideband RX, high-efficiency wideband TX, and excellent TX/RX isolation for 5G, LEO SATCOM, and JSAC applications. These three requirements interact and conflict with conventional designs.
motivation: Emerging mm-wave applications (5G, LEO, SATCOM, JSAC) demand wideband transceivers with incompatible performance goals that existing integrated TRX architectures cannot meet.
method: The chip combines three usually-conflicting functions in a single 65-nanometer CMOS chip: a sensitive receiver (adding only 3.3dB of noise—a measure where lower means cleaner signals), a powerful transmitter (reaching 20.2dBm output power), and isolation circuitry that prevents the transmitted signal from interfering with the received signal. It covers frequencies from 17.7 to 29.5 GHz by electronically tuning to whichever frequency is needed.
key_novelty: The key innovation is doing low-noise receiving, high-power transmitting, and transmit-receive isolation all in one wideband transceiver, rather than requiring separate narrowband designs.
contributions: Wideband transceiver achieving 3.3dB NF and 20.2dBm OP1dB across 17.7-29.5GHz
TX/RX isolation mechanism enabling simultaneous operation
65nm CMOS implementation with single tuning mechanism for wideband coverage
